note: Faithful rule manifest for operating and maintaining the Genesis repository, authored for the genesis-engineer agent. The .md is authoritative and unchanged; this indexes every actionable rule, typed checkable|judgment|principle, with a predicate (checkable) or reviewer_criterion (judgment). Grounded in THIS repo's real tooling (ci.yml, release.yml, bump-version.mjs, fetch-model.mjs, bin/genesis-memory.js, the three Cargo.toml, plugin.json, rust-toolchain.toml, the memory-sync skill + genesis:sync/fix/doctor/memory commands) plus the external primary specs (SemVer 2.0.0, Keep a Changelog 1.1.0, Cargo SemVer guide, GitHub Actions, Claude Code plugin/MCP docs, SQLite WAL backup). The autonomy/confirmation boundary is encoded as som-3 (wiring): no irreversible/outward-facing action runs unattended by default.

schema.section: source section the rule comes from
schema.text: faithful, imperative, scoped statement of the rule (same meaning as the source)
schema.type: checkable = a program can verify it | judgment = needs the independent reviewer | principle = governing rationale, not per-artifact checkable
schema.predicate: checkable only: {kind, spec} the hook/reviewer evaluates against produced artifacts
schema.reviewer_criterion: judgment only: the yes/no question the independent LLM-reviewer answers

rules.text: Optimize for reversibility and integrity: prefer local reversible actions, gate every outward-facing irreversible one, and treat every published release artifact as immutable and consumer-facing — a mistake is corrected by shipping a NEW version, never by editing a published one. (SemVer 2.0.0 clause 3.)

Verify every operational fact (the current release version, the CI gates, the pinned toolchain, the pinned model SHA) against a primary source in THIS repo before acting — the actual workflow YAML, script, Cargo.toml, plugin.json, or launcher constant — never a remembered or assumed value.

predicate.spec: operational values used in a decision are read from the concrete repo file (workflow/script/Cargo.toml/plugin.json/launcher) at decision time, not recalled or assumed; no action relies on an unverified value.

rules.text: THE autonomy boundary — never run an irreversible or outward-facing action (deploy, publish/release, git push or git push --force, create a release-triggering git tag v*, or delete data) without the user's explicit authorization.

predicate.spec: the agent requests confirmation before any deploy/publish/release, git push (or --force), release tag (v*), or data deletion; no such action occurs unattended by default.

rules.text: Let reversible, local, read-only actions proceed without a gate: build (cargo build --release), test, lint (clippy/fmt --check), dry-run, reading logs/state, fetching the model, and editing uncommitted working-tree files (a version bump, a changelog edit).

predicate.spec: actions classified as free (build/test/lint/dry-run/read/uncommitted working-tree edits) touch nothing outside the local working tree and require no confirmation; only the som-3 set is gated.

rules.text: Never force-push and never discard either side of a divergence; on a conflict you cannot resolve losslessly (JSONL left with <<<<<<< markers, unrelated histories, an unreconcilable push), STOP and consult the user.

predicate.spec: no code path runs git push --force / -f or resets away one side of a divergence; an unresolvable conflict halts and asks the user rather than discarding history.

rules.text: Before any gated action, present the exact command/diff and its blast radius (what changes, where it becomes visible — remote branch, public release, consumers' machines — and whether it is reversible), then wait for the go-ahead. Silence is not consent.

predicate.spec: each gated action is preceded by a stated plan/diff + blast-radius and an explicit user go-ahead before execution.

rules.text: Judge each requested operation's reversibility and blast radius to classify it as gated (som-3) or free (som-4); when in doubt, treat it as gated. Anything that leaves the machine, mutates shared history, or destroys data is gated; a local file edit is free.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Was each operation correctly classified by reversibility/blast-radius — gating everything that leaves the machine, mutates shared history, or deletes data, and defaulting to gated when uncertain — rather than acting first?

rules.text: Version per Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: MAJOR for incompatible/breaking changes, MINOR for backward-compatible new functionality (and whenever marking something deprecated), PATCH for backward-compatible bug fixes; a pre-release identifier (e.g. -beta) ranks BELOW the associated normal version; a released version is immutable — release a new one, never modify it.

predicate.spec: the chosen version bump matches the change class per SemVer 2.0.0 (major=breaking, minor=backward-compatible feature/deprecation, patch=backward-compatible fix); pre-release tags denote lower precedence; no published version is ever modified in place.

rules.text: Keep the release version in lockstep across its TWO sources of truth — .claude-plugin/plugin.json "version" and bin/genesis-memory.js RELEASE_VERSION — by running node scripts/bump-version.mjs <semver>; never hand-edit one without the other (the release gate refuses a mismatch).

predicate.spec: plugin.json version and launcher RELEASE_VERSION are always equal, set together via bump-version.mjs; a version change never edits one file alone.

rules.text: Treat the three Rust crate versions (server/cli/hook Cargo.toml, each 0.1.0, publish=false) as INTERNAL and decoupled from the consumer-facing release/plugin version (0.2.0-beta); do not conflate them and do not cargo publish the crates.

predicate.spec: crate versions are treated as internal (publish=false) and never used as, or synced to, the release/plugin version; no cargo publish of the crates is attempted.

rules.text: Cut a v<version> tag ONLY from a commit on main whose plugin.json version and launcher RELEASE_VERSION both equal the tag minus v; the release gate enforces the on-main ancestry + version match and refuses otherwise — satisfy the gate before tagging, never work around it. Flow: branch → merge to main → tag on main → release.

predicate.spec: a release tag is created only on a main-ancestor commit with plugin.json + launcher versions equal to the tag; the gate's on-main + version-match checks are satisfied, not bypassed.

rules.text: Cut a release in this fixed order: (1) green CI on the branch, (2) node scripts/bump-version.mjs <ver>, (3) update CHANGELOG, (4) merge to main, (5) tag v<ver> on main, (6) push the tag → release.yml gates/builds/publishes. Steps 4–6 (merge/tag/push) require the user's go-ahead (som-3).

predicate.spec: the release follows green-CI → bump → changelog → merge-main → tag → push in order, with the merge/tag/push boundary gated on user confirmation.

rules.text: Let CI (release.yml) perform the actual multi-platform build and publish — do not hand-build or hand-upload release assets; the pipeline builds self-contained binaries from the pure-Rust tract path (bundled SQLite, static Windows CRT) and verifies no dynamic inference-runtime sidecar is linked.

predicate.spec: release binaries + SHA256SUMS are produced and uploaded by release.yml (the 8-target build + self-contained/no-sidecar guard), not hand-built or hand-uploaded.

rules.text: Publish a pre-release tag (contains -, e.g. v0.2.0-beta) as a GitHub prerelease; publish only a final X.Y.Z tag as a full release. Never mark a -beta/-alpha/-rc build as a full release.

predicate.spec: a tag containing '-' publishes with --prerelease; a tag with no pre-release identifier publishes as a full release; the two are never swapped.

rules.text: Keep CI green: never merge to main or cut a release while ci.yml is red; a red main blocks every release (the gate builds from main). Fix or revert the offending change first.

predicate.spec: no merge-to-main or release proceeds while ci.yml is failing; a broken build is fixed or reverted before any outward step.

rules.text: Preserve every CI gate; never weaken, skip, or continue-on-error a gate to go green. Gates: server+hook+cli build+test on all three primary OSes; clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings + cargo fmt --check on hook and cli; node parse-check of every JS/MJS + plugin/launcher unit tests; the no-runtime-Python assertion; and the self-contained-binary regression guard.

predicate.spec: all ci.yml gates (3-OS rust build/test, clippy -D warnings + fmt --check on hook/cli, node parse-check + unit tests, python-free assertion, self-contained guard) remain enforced; none is disabled/continue-on-error to pass.

rules.text: Treat the pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml = 1.93.0) and pinned load-bearing deps (rusqlite =0.39.0, ort =2.0.0-rc.13, ort-tract =0.4.0) as deliberate pins with documented reasons; never bump them casually — a bump is a change to verify and test across all release targets.

predicate.spec: the pinned toolchain + load-bearing deps are changed only deliberately (with a documented reason) and re-verified across targets, never bumped as a convenience edit.

rules.text: Keep the embedding model pinned by revision + SHA-256 (scripts/fetch-model.mjs DEFAULT_REVISION + EXPECTED_MODEL_SHA256; fail-closed on mismatch); repointing the model requires --print-only capture AND regenerating the golden vectors + server embed::MODEL_* constants — never repoint it silently.

predicate.spec: the model revision+SHA stay pinned and fail-closed; any repoint regenerates golden vectors + server constants deliberately, never a silent revision change.

rules.text: Distribute ONLY via GitHub Release assets downloaded by the Node launcher — no npm, no registry account, no publish token; the release uses only the auto-provided GITHUB_TOKEN. Do not reintroduce npm publishing.

predicate.spec: release distribution is GitHub Release assets fetched by bin/genesis-memory.js using only GITHUB_TOKEN; no npm/registry publish path is present or reintroduced.

rules.text: SHA-256-verify every downloaded asset against the published SHA256SUMS before it is used; never serve or stage an unverified or mismatched asset (the launcher refuses an asset with no listed checksum or a mismatch).

predicate.spec: every fetched binary/model asset is hashed and compared to SHA256SUMS before use; a missing-checksum or mismatched asset is refused, never staged/served.

rules.text: Preserve /plugin update propagation: bump the plugin.json version on every consumer-facing change (an unbumped version ships no update), and rely on the launcher's --sync + .staged-version stamp to refresh already-bootstrapped repos to the plugin version.

predicate.spec: every consumer-facing change bumps plugin.json version so /plugin update ships it; the --sync/.staged-version mechanism that refreshes bootstrapped repos is left intact.

rules.text: Maintain the changelog in Keep a Changelog format: one dated entry per released version, newest first, changes grouped under Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed/Security, an Unreleased section at the top, and a stated note that the project follows Semantic Versioning; an entry exists for every version.

predicate.spec: the changelog has a top Unreleased section, dated newest-first version entries (one per version), grouped Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed/Security types, and a SemVer-adherence note.

rules.text: Write changelog entries for humans — user-visible impact, not a dump of git log lines — and mark a pulled release [YANKED].
rules.reviewer_criterion: Are the changelog entries human-readable, user-impact statements (not raw git-log dumps), with any pulled release marked [YANKED]?

rules.text: Keep the memory store's two artifacts consistent and BOTH committed, and never commit the sidecars: .genesis/memory.db is the ready vector store and source of truth; .genesis/memory/memory.jsonl is the diff-friendly mirror and merge safety-net (the .db self-heals from the JSONL on server start). Commit both together; never commit memory.db-wal / memory.db-shm.

predicate.spec: commits include both .genesis/memory.db and .genesis/memory/memory.jsonl together and never the WAL/shm sidecars; the .db is treated as source of truth with the JSONL as its self-healing mirror.

rules.text: Sync memory ONLY through the deterministic, lossless procedure (/genesis:sync / genesis-cli reconcile): commit both artifacts → fetch remote JSONL → UNION-reconcile keyed by (agent_id, text) (dedupe by content, never overwrite, never drop, stable-sorted + re-ided) → commit → push; consult the user only on a genuine git conflict; never force-push, never discard a side.

predicate.spec: memory sync runs commit-both → fetch → union-reconcile by (agent_id,text) → commit → push; it is lossless (no drop/overwrite) and only halts for a genuine git conflict, never force-pushing or discarding a side.

rules.text: Recover scattered memory via /genesis:doctor (read-only diagnosis) then /genesis:fix (consolidate THIS repo's agents' strays into the canonical .db), at a user-chosen scan scope, reading strays READ-ONLY; require an explicit --scope user|system or --root (never guess a scan area) and never pull a foreign repo's memory.

predicate.spec: stray recovery runs doctor (read-only) then fix at an explicit user-chosen scope, reads strays read-only, and consolidates only this repo's agents — never a foreign repo's memory, never a guessed scope.

rules.text: Do not file-copy the live memory DB for a backup while the server holds a WAL open (a raw cp mid-write can capture an inconsistent snapshot); for a consistent backup, checkpoint first, or back up via the JSONL export or SQLite's Online Backup API.

predicate.spec: a memory backup is taken via a WAL checkpoint + copy, the JSONL export, or the SQLite Online Backup API — never a plain file copy of an actively-written WAL database.

rules.text: Run /genesis:memory validate to check DB↔JSONL agreement and the embedding contract / drift canary; surface genuine contradictions to the user in the HTML report (full path given) and resolve WITH them — never auto-resolve silently and never serve a mixed-embedding-generation index (re-embed the whole store on a contract change).

predicate.spec: validate compares .db vs .jsonl and runs the embedding-contract/drift canary; contradictions are surfaced via the HTML report and resolved with the user, not auto-resolved; a mixed-generation index is re-embedded, never served.

rules.text: Roll back by rolling forward: because a published version is immutable, correct a bad release by shipping a fixed NEW version (or re-pointing the plugin version), never by editing a released tag or re-uploading over a published asset under the same version (consumer caches are per-version, so a same-version overwrite would not reach cached installs).

predicate.spec: a bad release is remediated by a new version (roll-forward), never by mutating a released tag/asset under the same version; per-version caching is respected.

rules.text: Verify a clean install on a real platform before declaring a release done, and let a straggler platform degrade gracefully: the release job publishes whatever built so one failing platform never sinks the rest, and the launcher treats a missing platform asset as a clear build-from-source path, not a crash.

predicate.spec: a release is confirmed by an actual clean-install verification (download → SHA verify → exec) on a target; a missing platform asset yields a build-from-source message and never blocks publishing the other platforms.

rules.text: Reproduce and diagnose a reported bug against a primary source (the real code / real output) before proposing a fix; never speculate a cause. Collect OS, Node/rustc versions, exact command, expected vs actual, and full output; a minimal reproduction outweighs a description.

predicate.spec: a fix is proposed only after the bug is reproduced/diagnosed against the real code or real output with the environment + repro captured — no speculative cause drives a change.

rules.text: Hold every change to the four hard rules (no shortcuts, no speculation, use the docs/expertise, production-ready + tested) and require a regression test: a bug fix ships a test that FAILS before the fix and PASSES after; new behavior ships with tests; the relevant CI gate passes before merge.

predicate.spec: each change satisfies the four hard rules; a bug fix carries a fail-before/pass-after regression test and new behavior carries tests; CI passes before merge.

rules.text: Route a security report or a committed secret PRIVATELY to the maintainer — never open, comment, or attach it on a public issue or PR.

predicate.spec: security vulnerabilities / leaked credentials are reported privately to the maintainer and never disclosed in the public issue/PR tracker.

rules.text: Track deferred and unsupported work in TODO.md with its reason and fix-path (e.g. linux-arm64-musl, win32-arm64 blocked upstream), and never claim an unbuilt platform is supported (consumers on it get a clean unsupported-platform message).

predicate.spec: deferred/unsupported items are recorded in TODO.md with reason + fix-path; supported-platform claims match what the release actually builds — no overstated coverage.

rules.text: Deprecate before you remove: announce with a MINOR bump + a CHANGELOG Deprecated entry, keep a migration path, then remove the capability in a later (breaking/major) release; never remove a consumer-facing capability without a deprecation trail.

predicate.spec: removing a consumer-facing capability is preceded by a deprecation (minor bump + CHANGELOG Deprecated entry + migration path); no capability is removed without that trail.

rules.text: Do not silently reverse a documented design decision (npm→GitHub-Releases distribution, .db-as-source-of-truth with .jsonl mirror, pure-Rust tract over ONNX Runtime); keep a superseded decision documented and surface a proposed reversal to the user rather than applying it unilaterally.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Was each documented design decision either upheld or its proposed reversal surfaced to the user (with the superseded decision kept documented), rather than silently flipped?

rules.text: Never write a credential/secret/key VALUE into any file, log, commit, changelog, or memory record — record 'credential present at <path>' instead — and never route around the genesis-hook gate that blocks credential shapes at write time.

predicate.spec: no authored artifact contains a credential/secret/key value; secrets are referenced as 'credential present at <path>'; the gate's credential-shape block is never bypassed.

rules.text: Use 'structured reasoning' in all authored text; never emit the banned reasoning-trace phrase the gate's regex rejects. Govern outputs and actions, not the private reasoning trace.

predicate.spec: authored text uses 'structured reasoning' and never emits the gate's banned reasoning-trace phrase; rules target outputs/actions, not the private reasoning trace.

rules.text: Honest limit: a green pipeline proves FORM (it built, published, and checksummed), not field correctness or safety on a consumer's machine — prove a release is good with a real clean-install verification and the user's sign-off, and never overstate 'shipped' as 'verified in the field'.
